reports.title: DIVIDEND DECLARATION - Wheaton Precious Metals Announces Quarterly Dividend

desk.headline: Revenue up 62% to $772m, beat; adjusted EPS $0.90 just short of estimates; 2026 production outlook unchanged

other.label: Cash operating margin per GEO sold

results: Revenue rose 62% to $772m on much higher gold and silver prices and 19% more ounces sold; adjusted EPS rose 46% to $0.90.
Production rose 13% to about 231,000 gold-equivalent ounces; silver jumped 37% as the Antamina stream from BHP kicked in, while gold slipped 8%.
Labour disputes hit San Dimas (from 18 Sep) and Stillwater (3 Sep–9 Oct), and Silvercorp's El Domo start slipped to 1 Nov 2027.
Cash costs averaged $548 per ounce, leaving a margin of $3,466 per ounce; operating cash flow was $645m and $372m of the credit line was repaid.
Net debt was about $1.5bn at quarter-end; the Q4 dividend was set at $0.195, up 18% on a year ago.

guidance.summary: Wheaton kept its 2026 production forecast and its long-term plan to reach about 1.2m gold-equivalent ounces a year by 2030.

points: Management called the 2026 production range achievable and expects a strong fourth quarter, with Salobo gold output improving as grades recover.
The growth plan to 1.2m ounces by 2030 does not rely on buying new streams; Antamina, Blackwater, Koné and Kurmuk are the main drivers.
Koné is expected to deliver over 50,000 oz in 2027 and over 60,000 oz in 2028; Kurmuk under 10,000 oz in 2027.
Management noted the long-term outlook is sensitive to the gold-to-silver price ratio.
call.source: Quartr Q3 2026 call summary, 6 Nov 2026, and the Q3 results news release

watch: Whether the San Dimas and Stillwater disputes dent Q4 output enough to threaten the 2026 range.
Ramp-up at Koné and the Antamina stream, and timing of El Domo.
How the gold and silver prices hold up, since they drove most of the revenue jump.
